#3141. Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft could reshape enterprise spending, but there's a critical difference between estimated value and money saved.

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:

This means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

#3140. One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Apple's folding phone is showing unmistakable signs of wear, but it hasn't broken yet.

Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago. Every day since then, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, a dedicated machine inside CNET’s lab has been folding and unfolding it over and over again. For science.

How many times can we fold the iPhone Duo? As of Friday, Nov. 20, we’re up to more than 565,000 folds and the Duo hasn’t broken yet. The hinge has shown signs of potential failure, however. Our technicians, as well as the cameras and sensors that are part of our testing rig, continue to monitor the situation and collect data.

I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky. My team and I designed and built this proprietary machine to test foldable phones like Apple’s and its Samsung rival, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which we’ve also started testing). I’ve worked on the methodology and build of this testing rig for months in anticipation of Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone.

We even named our machine to match its purpose: Meet the Fold-a-Phone.

My team of engineers and testing experts has been watching the iPhone Duo open and close, over and over, for the past few weeks to rigorously and systematically monitor the durability of Apple’s hinge and two screens.

After all, repeatedly folding a phone with bare hands can only get you so far in understanding the complex forces at play between the magnetics that snap the screen shut and the all-critical hinge.

CNET’s Senior Technology Reporter, Abrar Al-Heeti, has done a beautiful job capturing the iPhone Duo’s pros and cons in her smart, thorough review as well as her one-month-later follow-up. Our Fold-a-Phone machine will add a deep data foundation to complement her real-world experience.

Since Apple hasn’t publicly shared claims of the iPhone Duo’s foldable lifespan, CNET’s Fold-a-Phone machine is poised to provide a wealth of valuable data about Apple’s first foldable phone and competing models in the foldable market.

And yes, you’d better believe we will use our treasure trove of in-house data to share status updates and comparisons during our ongoing testing window with the Duo.

Join CNET’s iPhone Duo livestream on YouTube weekdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. ET, where you can follow along live and watch the Fold-a-Phone do its thing to a Duo.

The importance of this moment is hard to overstate. Apple’s appearance on the foldable smartfold frontier lags Samsung by seven years (the first Galaxy Fold went on sale in the US in September 2019). Motorola and other phone-makers have long experimented with foldable phones in every shape and size, including a trifold accordion foldable phone we first demoed in 2019.

CNET’s mobile experts, including Al-Heeti and Editor at Large Andrew Lanxon, have discussed the legitimizing effect of the iPhone Duo’s existence on the entire foldable phone landscape, which has previously felt like a new-wave fantasy rather than a mainstream riptide.

In many ways, Apple’s newfound competition with existing foldable phones completes the portfolio. That is precisely why we’re building the Fold-a-Phone now, and why our proprietary machine, methodology and test data will enrich our collective understanding of the capabilities – and yes, limitations – of foldable phones as our true next-generation mobile device.

Most current foldable phones are rated for 200,000 to 500,000 folds. As such, we knew we needed to create a robust and adaptable machine that could accommodate book- and flip-style foldable phones of any size, dimension and hinge orientation. (Note: The Fold-a-Phone was not built for trifold phones, which present a unique element to the engineering challenge.)

Moreover, we wanted to test the phone the way people would actually use it. No one just sits around opening and closing their foldable phone at top speed all day. Rather, you open it naturally, spend a few minutes watching a video, browsing a web page, or using an app, close it, and then put it in your pocket. This may happen dozens of times per day.

Mimicking this usage on the Fold-a-Phone limits undue stress on the phone hinge and avoids generating excess heat compared to a test built for speed.

We determined that a cadence of roughly 4 seconds could sidestep technical hurdles while also being reasonably fast. The foldable phone takes 1 second to open, 1 second to fully open, 1 second to close and 1 second to fully close. This cycle counts as a single completed fold. Then, the cycle repeats until either the hinge or the screen gives out.

In conceptualizing and building the Fold-a-Phone, our team has used standard, off-the-shelf components to simplify the machine’s development. The essential design consists of two armatures, distinctly designed to perform the opening and closing movements with both force and grace.

An industrial-grade stepper motor drives each armature, with the host software (running on a connected computer) deterministically adjusting the torque to complete each step of the process while also protecting the phone. If any of the several proximity sensors fail to detect the armature in the correct position, the machine stops immediately.

We also monitor the motors’ power usage to track how well the foldable phone opens and closes over time. We have set up cameras to capture images and video of the test from multiple angles, and we will analyze regular status updates from the computer to determine the current status of the phone and the test.

To ensure we never miss a major development, the entire rig is connected to an EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus power station to guard against electricity outages, and all the output data is saved to multiple locations.

To secure each phone to the machine, we use our CNET Lab Test-winning 3D printer, the Prusa Core One, to 3D-print a custom “sled” that matches each phone’s exact dimensions. We secure the phone to the sled with heavy-duty double-sided tape (yes, it works!) and then screw the sled onto the machine.

There’s always room for improvement. We’re constantly looking for ways to make the machine run more smoothly and quietly without disrupting the folding rhythm.

Apple’s presence is already changing the game and could very well spur innovation in ways we can’t predict today. But until then, our Fold-a-Phone machine will continue to test the iPhone Duo and its competitors, and CNET’s writers will report on how well these individual hinged devices stand up to the challenge – or fold under pressure.

The company also released new ROI tracking tools for companies monitoring their AI spend.

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

#3137. The Stock Market Sounds an Alarm as Investors Get Bad News About President Donald Trump's Economy

The stock market could decline sharply as persistent inflation and rich valuations fuel investor anxiety.

By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:21AM EST

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›

The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) delivered positive returns for much of 2026, supported by strong corporate earnings and enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence. But both indexes recently entered market correction territory, falling more than 10% from their respective highs.

Unfortunately, the situation could get worse. Investors recently received troubling updates about President Donald Trump's economy: Inflation accelerated in September, and subsequent estimates suggest pricing pressures have continued to intensify. Meanwhile, the stock market is sounding an alarm last seen during the dot-com bubble.

President Donald Trump sits with his hands clasped during a meeting at the White House, surrounded by administration officials. Image source: Official White House Photo.

Inflation accelerated in September, complicating the Federal Reserve's effort to restore price stability. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 3.7% from the previous year, up from 3.4% in August and the highest reading since May.

Research from the Federal Reserve Banks of St. Louis and Minneapolis helps explain why prices are rising more quickly. President Trump's tariffs were the primary driver of inflation earlier in the year, but supply shocks driven by energy sector prices have since become the primary culprit. The Iran war has disrupted Middle Eastern oil shipments, pushing crude oil prices and transportation costs higher.

Unfortunately, the inflation outlook remains troubling. The Cleveland Fed estimates that headline CPI inflation is trending toward 3.9% in November. And core CPI inflation (which excludes volatile food and energy prices) is projected to accelerate to 2.9%, up from 2.6% in September, suggesting that elevated energy prices are spreading to other areas of the economy.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate in September, the first rate hike in three years, but investors expect another rate hike in December due to persistent inflation. That bodes ill for the stock market because higher interest rates increase borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, potentially slowing economic growth and creating a drag on corporate profits. They also make bonds more attractive relative to stocks, which can put downward pressure on equity valuations.

The price-to-earnings (PE) ratio is one of the most widely used equity valuation metrics. It divides a company's share price by its earnings per share from the last 12 months. But the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio takes a different approach, dividing the inflation-adjusted price by the average inflation-adjusted earnings from the last decade. That methodology smooths fluctuations in corporate profits caused by the business cycle.

The S&P 500's CAPE ratio was 40.1 in October, marking the sixth straight monthly reading above 40. Previously, the index's CAPE ratio last exceeded 40 during the dot-com crash in September 2000. Unfortunately, such rich valuations have often preceded dismal returns, as shown in the table below.

Historically, following months in which the S&P 500's CAPE ratio exceeded 40, the index returned an average of 0% over the next six months; it declined by an average of 3% over the next year; and it declined by an average of 19% over the next two years. In other words, history suggests the stock market is headed much lower.

However, one limitation of the CAPE ratio is its backward-looking nature. It does not incorporate forward earnings estimates, meaning it may overstate valuations when corporate profits are growing quickly. Artificial intelligence has already contributed to higher profit margins and higher earnings growth across the S&P 500, and that trend is projected to continue.

Additionally, the historical returns shown in the table reflect overlapping periods during the dot-com bubble, rather than numerous independent market episodes. Consequently, they illustrate the risks associated with extreme valuations, but do not definitively predict what will happen next.

Nevertheless, investors should not dismiss this warning entirely The stock market remains expensive by historical standards, and the prospect of higher interest rates could put additional pressure on valuations. Together, those headwinds could push the S&P 500 into a bear market. If that happens, remember that dips have historically been great buying opportunities: The S&P 500 has rebounded from every past drawdown.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

After spending months training with firefighters in the field, the app uses Google Gemini to decode distorted radio signals in real time.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

On Friday, Google’s Gemini team announced the results of a new partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

The Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to update maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

“This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” said Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google says the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

One metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

The Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

The integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

#3135. Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company announced at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#3134. Don’t Miss Out on GTA 6 Launch Week: Here’s How to Take Rockstar’s New Game Anywhere

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Whether you’re on a work trip, vacationing or otherwise indisposed, there are a few good options to scratch your Grand Theft Auto itch on the go.

Look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may currently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

If you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

If you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

The PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

Microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing new game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

#3133. Where Will Micron Stock Be in 3 Years?

Micron's stock has plunged in recent months, but the next three years could still be lucrative.

By Keith Speights – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:26AM EST

Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost nearly half its market cap in five months. That's the bad news. The good news is that the semiconductor stock is still up nearly 120% year-to-date.

Wall Street thinks that Micron has a lot of room to run. The consensus 12-month price target reflects a potential upside of around 160%. But where will Micron stock be in three years? There are three potential scenarios.

The bull case for Micron is that its stock soars to between $1,800 and $2,200 by late 2029, a gain of 3.2x at the midpoint of the range. To make this scenario possible, the demand for the company's memory chips would need to remain strong over the next several years. In addition, the humanoid robot market would need to gain momentum. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said in the company's fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings call that he expects a "sustained, substantial multi-decade memory demand cycle" to begin later this decade.

The base case is that the stock jumps to $1,100 to $1,400. Micron's share price would roughly double at the midpoint of this range. The high-bandwidth memory (HBM) market would need to continue growing robustly in this scenario. It also assumes that Chinese memory chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) gains only modest market share with its HBM chips. However, Micron probably wouldn't require the humanoid robot market to pick up significant steam for the base case to be achieved.

What's the bear case? Micron's stock declines to a range of $400 to $600 over the next three years. The most likely way this scenario could unfold is if CXMT advances its HBM technology faster than expected and changes the market dynamics. An influx of HBM supply could trigger a price war among major HBM suppliers. As Micron's margins fall, so would its share price. A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending could also weigh on Micron's stock. With many investors already nervous about hyperscalers' massive AI-related capital expenditures and a growing public backlash against AI data centers in the U.S., such a slowdown isn't out of the question.

Micron is still a cyclical stock. Any of the three scenarios is possible, depending on the duration and intensity of the current memory chip boom. That said, if I had to predict where Micron stock will actually be three years from now, it would be around the lower end of the base-case range.

I fully expect the demand for HBM to remain strong. Whether the humanoid robot market becomes a significant tailwind for Micron between now and 2029 remains to be seen, though. As for CXMT, I think the company will be a key player in HBM. However, I don't anticipate that Micron's growth will be derailed because of increased competition. A cumulative gain of 80% or more for Micron over the next three years seems attainable, in my view.

5 tips to get you the best big-screen TV deal this Black Friday

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

TV deals are one of the best parts of Black Friday, and if you’re vigilant, you’ve probably already noticed discounts starting to trickle in. If you’ve been eyeing a big-screen TV and waiting for your moment to strike, this is probably the best time of year to buy one.

But making a big purchase like a TV is also where a bad deal can cost you the most. A huge discount can look great on paper, and it’s easy to miss the fine print when the low price tag grabs all your attention. You’ll save money now, but if you buy the wrong TV for you, you may find yourself annoyed months later when you realize you picked up a model with the wrong panel, weak gaming specs, or another personal deal-breaker.

So, let’s not spoil your Thanksgiving dinner, and make sure you get the best TV deal you can this Black Friday. Before you add anything to your cart, here are five things I’d check first.

If you're looking for a TV that delivers fast action and flawless detail, the UR8 RGB MiniLED TV from Hisense creates natural color that's closer to real life. Its AI processor will adjust the picture in real time, balancing it without any manual setup, so sunsets look warm and skin tones look natural. The 180Hz motion processing reduces blur so you can clearly see what's going on, whether it's in a fast-moving action movie or the latest AAA video game.

When you start TV shopping, try not to get bogged down by the “was” price you’ll see in big, bold letters on the product page. Instead, treat it as context. The “was” price is usually just the TV’s launch MSRP, and plenty of TVs sell for well below it for most of their shelf lives. What matters most is the current price compared to what the TV cost in September and October of 2026, so pull up a price tracker before you pull the trigger. If the deal doesn’t beat its most recent price, it isn’t really a deal.

Older models are also where a lot of the deepest discounts hide. Retailers still have last year’s stock to clear, and we’ve even noted that 2025 TVs may be the safer buy this year considering recent tech price hikes. Double-check what you’d give up by going with an older version. Sometimes it’s something inconsequential like a tiny bit of brightness. Or, sometimes it’s something you really care about, like a faster refresh rate for gaming.

Consider where you’ll actually put the TV before you buy it, because the room will determine the panel you need. OLED is always my pick for a dark room. But if your living room gets a lot of natural light, brightness and glare resistance will matter more, and that’s where Mini-LED shines. It gets brighter, usually costs less per inch, and some models have screens built to fight reflections. The anti-glare screen on the Hisense U6SF Pro I reviewed stood out.

There’s a middle lane, too. QLED TVs are usually the budget-friendly option, with bright, punchy color for less money. The tradeoff is that they typically have fewer dimming zones than a Mini-LED, so blacks can look a bit grayer when you turn the lights down.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

As an avid gamer, this is the part of the spec sheet I read first. Look for native 120Hz or 144Hz panels, variable refresh rate (VRR), and the number of HDMI 2.1 ports. A TV can say “4K at 144Hz” and still offer only two HDMI 2.1 ports. That’s totally fine if you have just one or two gaming consoles. But toss in another device and a soundbar, and you’ll run out of room fast. So, take stock of all your gear first to figure out the configuration you need. If you can get a TV with four HDMI 2.1 ports, that’s pretty much the best-case scenario.

While you’re at it, check the TV’s OS, too, since you’ll be using it to navigate your content every day. There’s no wrong choice between Roku, Fire TV (Vega OS), and Google TV, but if you’d rather not relearn a remote, it’s worth knowing which one comes in the box. Personally, I like Roku TVs for their streamlined simplicity, but your mileage may vary.

When it comes to TVs, the price tag is just the beginning. TV speakers are usually not great, and the bigger the screen is, the more you’ll notice. I’d plan on snagging one of the best soundbars with pretty much any set. Make sure there’s room for it, though, because some TVs sit pretty low, and a soundbar can end up blocking the bottom of the picture or the sensor. Also, please don’t forget to measure your space. Make sure to check the TV stand width against your media console (lots of big TVs have feet way out at the edges), the doorway, and the wall if you’re mounting it.

I’d also think twice about any extended warranty pitches at checkout. They aren’t always a bad idea, but check what the manufacturer’s warranty already includes first. While you’re at it, I’d also check the return window. Some retailers stretch theirs for the holidays, but some don’t, and January is a bad time to find that out.

Conventional wisdom says that TV prices bottom out around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but this year comes with an asterisk. Chips and panels have both gotten pricier, and there aren’t many signs that will change anytime soon. That doesn’t mean prices won’t drop later this month, but it does mean the price floor might be a bit higher than you remember. So if a TV passes the first four checks and the price makes you happy, I’d buy it now. Holding out for another $100 off is how people end up missing out on the TV they really want.

My rule of thumb is to set a maximum price before I start scrolling, and set a price alert for the model(s) I want. It’ll keep the countdown timers and “only 3 left!” banners from making the final decision for you. Also, ask about the store’s price adjustment policy—some will refund the difference if the price drops within a set window.

If you end up missing the best deal, don’t panic. Cyber Monday is right after Black Friday, and TVs often go on sale well into December. The catch is that popular sizes of the best models tend to sell out first. Ultimately, the best Black Friday TV deal is the one that best fits your room and budget.

Dylan Haas is a Freelance Contributor and Lab Tester for Tom’s Guide. He’s a seasoned journalist with bylines at publications like Mashable, GameSpot, and Paste Magazine where he covered the latest in tech, gaming, and entertainment.

#3131. I’ve tested Ubuntu 27.04 ahead of its April release – and it will wow you

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

I've been using Ubuntu 27.04, and the speed boost is noticeable. Here's what else is coming.

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful

One thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:

With the repository added, you can install it with:

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Also: Linux has hundreds of distros: 5 reasons to stop using the same few

It’s been a very long time since Canonical had a disappointing release, and 27.04 will keep up that trend.

#3130. What Every 60-Year-Old Should Know About Social Security

Turning 60? Now’s the time to start thinking about Social Security.

By Keith Speights – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:44AM EST

I suspect that nearly every American who is 60 is already thinking about retirement -- as they should. And that involves contemplating upcoming decisions about Social Security. Making the right choices can have lifelong implications.

There's still plenty of time to finalize those decisions, but it's not too soon to begin thinking about them. Here are five things every 60-year-old should know about Social Security.

No Social Security decision is more important than choosing when you claim benefits. If you're 60, you could file for benefits within the next two years. However, make sure you understand the trade-offs of claiming before your full retirement age (FRA) of 67.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) will reduce benefits by around 30% for anyone who claims at age 62. And the early-retirement penalty is permanent. Your benefits will only increase with annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs). On the other hand, holding off until age 70 to claim Social Security will increase your benefits by 24% compared with claiming at 67.

Many people will decide the advantages of claiming at 62 are worth forgoing the higher monthly benefits. That's especially true for those who don't expect to live past their late 70s. There isn't a one-size-fits-all right decision. Every person needs to fully consider all factors for their personal situation.

Putting aside the early-retirement penalties and delayed-retirement credits, working longer could increase your Social Security benefit for another reason. SSA calculates your benefit using the 35 years with your highest earnings, adjusted for inflation. Many earn significantly more in the last few years of their careers than they did early on. Those higher-earnings years can replace the lower-earnings ones and boost your Social Security benefit.

This is even more important for anyone with fewer than 35 years of earnings. If you don't have at least a 35-year earnings record, SSA will plug zeros in for the missing years in its benefits calculation.

Speaking of earnings records, it's a good idea to start checking them before you claim benefits. There could be errors that affect how much you receive from Social Security. You can create a "my Social Security" account at SSA.gov and log in to it to verify that your earnings record is accurate.

If you spot a potential problem, check with SSA about what supporting documentation you'll need to get it fixed. Getting your earnings record correct at age 60 could spare you major headaches later after you claim benefits.

Don't think that the decisions you make about Social Security only impact you. They can also affect your spouse.

For example, the higher-earning spouse's claiming age permanently sets the survivor benefits available to the other spouse if the higher-earning spouse dies first. Coordinating when each spouse claims Social Security benefits is an important step that shouldn't be overlooked.

Benjamin Franklin wrote that "nothing can be said to be certain, except death and taxes." Unfortunately, his statement is still applicable -- even for Social Security benefits, in some cases.

Up to 85% of your Social Security benefits could be subject to federal income taxes depending on your combined income, which is calculated by summing your adjusted gross income, nontaxable interest, and half of your Social Security benefits. The thresholds where federal taxes begin to kick in are $25,000 for single filers and $32,000 for married couples.

Currently, 42 states plus the District of Columbia don't tax Social Security benefits. However, if you live in Colorado, Connecticut, Minnesota, Montana, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Utah, or Vermont, some of your Social Security income may be subject to tax.

The good news if you're 60 is that you don't have to make any Social Security decisions immediately. The bad news is that time flies. Starting to think about retirement and Social Security now could pay off later.

#3129. iOS 27.3 Could Bring the Redesigned Health App and a More Capable Siri AI to Your Device Soon

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems

The Health app overhaul and new Apple Intelligence features lead the latest public beta.

Apple launched the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the new Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS update in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a new Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by new audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

While both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I said, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just said.

Siri AI gets a huge update in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

You can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

StandBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

Apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

If you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a new setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

If you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have new options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

Next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

Those are a few of the new features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

#3128. Your Wear OS smartwatch just got a new way to save battery life

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

It could make your Pixel Watch or Samsung Galaxy Watch more power efficient.

Some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving update. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch users can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s new model worth it?

Constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how quickly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future

The update improves battery life without users having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

That’s not the only Google Play Services update that Wear OS smartwatch users can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

#3126. Live Now! The iPhone Duo’s Hinge Keeps Going After 565K Folds in Our Machine

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

In our fourth week of nonstop folding, the iPhone Duo's hinge is still opening and closing but with mixed performance.

As we continue our fourth week of folding Apple’s iPhone Duo in our custom Fold-a-Phone machine, the $1,999 foldable phone has surpassed 565,000 folds and it’s showing. While the Duo is still capable of opening and closing, on our Tuesday livestream you can see that the phone is having difficulty staying closed. #3125. Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX Each Formed a Special Committee to Explore a Merger as His AI Spending Accelerates. Here's Why Combining Them Could Reshape How Investors Value Tesla's Robotaxi Business.

A Tesla-SpaceX merger could give the automaker's robotaxi business a boost.

By Lyle Daly – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:00AM EST

Last month, Tesla (TSLA -7.64%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) each formed a special committee of independent directors to consider a merger. Elon Musk, the CEO and largest individual shareholder of both companies, can't participate in the talks.

A deal would combine the top space company and automaker by market cap. For Tesla investors, the biggest change may be how the market values the company's robotaxi business.

Although both companies are richly valued, SpaceX stock has the higher market cap and valuation. It's worth $2 trillion and trades at 58 times trailing sales, as of Nov. 19. Tesla has a market cap of $1.5 trillion and trades at 13 times trailing sales.

Tesla's valuation is largely tied to humanoid robots, robotaxis, and AI services such as full self-driving (FSD). But cars are still the core business, and Tesla's operating income declined 56% year over year to $718 million in Q3 2026. Currently, robotaxi is part of a car company, which weighs on how the market can value it.

A merger would put robotaxi inside a company with a rapidly growing AI business, with revenue that skyrocketed 830% year over year to $7.6 billion in Q3. Investors could start valuing it as an AI business, not an add-on to a car business.

Robotaxi is an expensive business that requires vehicles, chips, compute resources, and connectivity. Tesla's network is also expanding quickly, with nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised miles logged by the end of September, growing about eightfold from the previous quarter. As the network grows, costs will continue to increase.

SpaceX is spending heavily on AI, reporting $48.1 billion in capital expenditures over the first nine months of 2026. It's guiding for another $35 billion to $40 billion in Q4. Tesla is pulling back, revising its capex guidance down to about $20 billion in 2026, from more than $25 billion. SpaceX could provide the robotaxi business with more funding, its existing AI infrastructure, and connectivity through the Starlink network, all contributing to faster expansion.

Although robotaxi is an exciting business, it's not yet making a financial impact. Musk doesn't expect it to make a noticeable difference to Tesla's finances until around Q2 2027, and that may be an optimistic viewpoint. He previously expected robotaxi service to be widespread across the U.S. by the end of 2026. Tesla offers service in nine metro areas, so it's a long way to go, showing how reality often falls well short of expectations.

If there's a merger, robotaxi will become part of a company potentially worth $3.5 trillion or more. Investors could have a harder time tracking robotaxi's progress than they do now.

Merger talks are in the early stages, with no proposed terms. Tesla would also need approval from a majority of all outstanding shares, not just those voting, because Musk doesn't control the company's voting power as he does with SpaceX. A merger could make robotaxi a more valuable business, but for now, what's important is that it starts producing meaningful revenue in 2027.

Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training

Anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

According to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.)

The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

Like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

If you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:

This will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

To prevent Claude from creating new memories from your conversations:

If you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

However, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

#3119. This Pipeline Partnership Raised Its Payout by 12.5% for the Third Straight Year. Here’s How Much Longer It Can Keep That Up.

MPLX can still afford to fund its massive distributions.

MPLX (MPLX -1.27%), a midstream company spun off from Marathon Petroleum (MPC -0.20%) in 2012, operates over 10,000 miles of crude oil and light-product pipelines in 14 states. It pays a forward yield of 8.9%, and it's raised its annual payout by 12.5% for three consecutive years.

MPLX is a master limited partnership (MLP) that passes its taxable income through to investors rather than paying federal corporate income tax. These distributions are often treated in part as a return of capital, which reduces an investor's cost basis and defers their taxes until the position is sold. That structure can be more tax-efficient than earning dividends from traditional corporations, but it requires investors to report an additional K-1 tax form every year.

MLPs cover their distributions (not dividends) with their distributable cash flow (DCF). MPLX spent 64%, 65.3%, and 71.5% of its annualized DCF on distributions in 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. That ratio declined as it ramped up its investments and acquisitions in 2025, but it can probably still afford to raise its annual distributions for at least the next few years.

MPLX has already generated a total return of 179% over the past five years, but it could still have more upside potential if oil prices stay elevated and its pipeline volumes hold steady. It's well-insulated from volatile oil prices -- since it merely charges companies "tolls" to use its infrastructure -- and it should remain a reliable income play for the foreseeable future.

Meta's 2026 sustainability report isn't a glowing review, thanks to AI.

Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Big Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the company is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”

It’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, said in 2023 that the company’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”

Meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the company says. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

Take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its new data center designs compared to its original ones.

But, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The company also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

#3115. Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Encryption can't protect your messages from an AI agent peeking over your shoulder.

Don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

Whittaker said that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the company is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

The problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal says that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

Whittaker said the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how big tech AI agents work.

“Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker said. “This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”

In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

“So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” said Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

Strand said the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand said.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

#3112. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

No space agency has ever staged spacecraft in orbit for a year before sending them on to Mars.

NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the company was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.
